- `current_frame.step` is the current environment step count.
- `current_frame.level` is the current level number.
- `current_frame.shape` is a `(rows, cols)` tuple.
- The raw numeric grid is intentionally not exposed. - You have exactly one tool: `python`.
- When calling `python`, emit exactly the tool-call format shown elsewhere in this prompt for this model. - The `python` tool code is not saved between calls, so rewrite any custom utility logic you still need.

In other words, one of those 6 clicks (21,19 / 35,9 / 31,20 / 31,10 / 19,23 / 20,18) toggled the bar H→V!
Which one? The dark red (31,20)? The gray mat (31,10)? Or the corner of the top slot (20,18)?
2. Red table click did nothing to the bar (V→V)?? It used to toggle! Wait — "after red table click: C V" — no bar change! Previously the red table click was H↔V. Hmm!! Did the red table click stop toggling? Or… wait a moment, maybe the red click actually toggled V→H→… no, a single click is one toggle.
Wait, maybe I misread the bar at the start. Let me check: at the end of the previous batch (after the 6-click test), the image showed the bar as V (vertical red in the center) — yes! The image at step 125 showed the vertical red bar. So after the 6-click batch, the bar was V. Before the batch it was H. So yes, one of those 6 clicks toggled the bar!
And now the red table click: no bar change (V→V)!! Previously (first 2 batches) the red table click was toggling. What changed??
Hmm wait — in the batch before that: "red click -> H" (V→H worked). Then the 6-click batch: one click toggled H→V. Now the red table click: no change.
Could it be… the red table click doesn't toggle the bar, and instead the piece click (31,15 red piece) is what toggles?! Let me re-verify the evidence:
- Batch 2 (5 actions): A frame click no-op; B red table click (18,48): diff included bar change (129-diff included bar? the diff's bbox rows 16-63 cols 1-55 — frame removal + ??? Let me re-verify: the first 14 entries of the diff were frame cells (16,44..52 W→B, 17,44 W→B, 17,52, 18,44, 18,52, 19,41…). 129 cells = frame 40×2 (two tables, both frames removed at once? no — the red click removed both frames? W40 both disappeared at transition 12 (red click). 40+40=80 frame cells + bar cells. H bar 24 cells → V bar 24 cells, overlap 4×4? H = rows 30-33 cols 12-27 (24 cells), V = rows 24-37? cols 18-21. Overlap = rows 30-33 cols 18-21 = 16 cells. Changed = 24+24-2×16 = 20. 80+20=100 ≠ 129. Plus timer. Hmm, 129-100 = 29… the dark red also moves? The dark red is a fixed 16. Gray? Whatever — the red table click diff included the bar toggle (in the image at step 104, after action B, the bar was vertical: yes, the image at step 104 showed the vertical red).
- So red table click: toggled at step 104 (H→V? at that time the bar was H (initial), after click → V ✓ image shows V ✓).
- Batch 3: "red click -> H" (step ~112): V→H ✓ (at that point I wasn't outputting an image; the subsequent image at step 119 shows the horizontal bar ✓).
- 6-click batch: bar H→V (one of the clicks).
- Now: red table click: no toggle (V→V).
So the red table click toggles sometimes and not others?! Or the bar toggling is due to something else, and the correlation was coincidental?
Wait, another possibility: the red table click is what toggles the bar, but the toggle only works when the bar is in a specific state… V→V? That would be "toggle only from H." First click: H→V ✓. Second: V→H ✓ (works from V). Third: V→V ✗. Contradiction.
Or the bar toggle is due to the piece click (31,15): in batch 3 I clicked the red piece (31,15) in the target test — at that time the bar was H, after the batch… the image at step 119 shows H. Hmm, no change from the piece click.
Ugh. Let me carefully identify which of the 6 clicks in batch 4 toggled the bar. That batch: (21,19), (35,9), (31,20), (31,10), (19,23), (20,18). I output swap_state each time but not the bar! Damn. But the swap stayed C throughout. Bar: H before the batch, V after. One of these 6 toggled the bar.
Candidates: (31,20) dark red — part of the red assembly! (31,10) gray — part of the red assembly (leftmost gray of the H bar row? H bar row = gray (30,8-11) + red (30,12-17) + dark red (30,18-21): yes (31,10) is the gray part of the red row!). (19,23) top gray mat. (20,18) corner of the top slot. (21,19) / (35,9) = blue piece (probably no-op).
Hypothesis: clicking the red assembly (any of its cells: gray/red/dark red) toggles the bar H/V. And the red table click is… what is it? Maybe the red table click removed the frame and does nothing else now (frame is already removed → no-op). But batch 2's B (red table click) had a 129-cell diff including the bar… or did it? Let me re-verify: was the bar really V in the step 104 image? The image at step 104 (after 5 actions): vertical red bar — yes, I remember. Before (step 100 image): horizontal red bar. So the red table click at step 103-104 did indeed toggle H→V (along with removing the frame).
So: red table click #1: toggle + frame removal. Red table click #2 (step 112): toggle V→H (no frame, no problem). Red table click #3 (just now): no toggle?!
What's different?? Step parity? Or… the bar position relative to green? Or the timer?
Hmm, wait, maybe I should look at the actual diff of the red click I just did. Let me inspect the last transition's diff. Also, I need to re-verify the bar state detection: 'R' pixels==24 → bar. Could the R node have become a different pixel count? If the bar is V: rows 24-37? V bar = 14 tall × 4 wide, cols 18-21. In the step 128 image: vertical red at cols ~18-21, rows ~24-37 ✓ 24 px.
Let me examine the diff of the last transition, and also re-test the red table click right now (another toggle?).
